newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - Data show economy not out of control.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - Data show economy not out of control.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday that the latest official economic figures showed the UK economy was not running out of control and the current account was almost in balance.
"Today we have national accounts showing a savings ratio running at a historically high level for a period of growth. This boom is not a consumer bubble," Clarke said in a statement.

The Office for National Statistics said revised fourth quarter gross domestic product data showed growth of 0.8 percent on the quarter and 2.6 percent year-on-year. A savings ratio of 11.6 percent was seen in the fourth quarter.
On top of that, a fourth quarter current account surplus of 873 million stg left a deficit of just 14 million stg for 1996 as a whole.

"These are excellent figures showing the current account almost in balance," Clarke said. "They show that this time we have healthy growth which is not running into the balance of payments problems which caused past booms to turn into bust."
